blocks.text: In the definition of work it is not clear whether the same amount of work is done in one second or in one hour; the rate at which work is done is often of interest in practical applications.

blocks.title: Power
blocks.text: Power is the measure of the rate at which work is being done. If work delta W is done in a time interval delta t, the average power P_av during the interval is P_av = delta W / delta t ... (4.6). If work is expressed as a function of time, the instantaneous power P at any instant is P = limit (delta t -> 0) delta W / delta t ... (4.7), where delta W is the work done in the short interval delta t.

Since delta W = F . delta d, P = F . delta d / delta t = F . (delta d / delta t), and since delta d / delta t = v, P = F . v ... (4.8). The SI unit of power is the watt, defined as one joule of work done in one second. Sometimes, for example in electrical measurements, the unit of work is expressed as the watt second; a commercial unit of electrical energy is the kilowatt-hour, the work done in one hour by an agency whose power is one kilowatt: 1 kW h = 1000 W x 3600 s, or 1 kW h = 3.6 x 10^6 J = 3.6 MJ.

blocks.title: Example 4.2
blocks.text: A 70 kg man runs up a long flight of stairs in 4.0 s; the vertical height of the stairs is 4.5 m. Calculate his power output in watts. Solution: work done = mgh, power = mgh / t = (70 kg x 9.8 m s^-2 x 4.5 m) / 4 s = 7.7 x 10^2 kg m^2 s^-3 = 7.7 x 10^2 W.
It takes about 9 x 10^9 J of energy to make a car, and the car then uses about 1 x 10^12 J of energy from petrol in its lifetime (Do You Know).
